Audio Priority Bar 2.11.0 adds Shortcuts actions to pick the output or microphone, mute it, and turn automatic switching on or off, and gives the app its own icon. Coming from 2.10.0, the update installs in place, and your existing priorities and overrides are kept.

## Shortcuts

- The Shortcuts app now lists four actions: **Set Output**, **Set Microphone**, **Set Microphone Mute** and **Set Automatic Switching**. Picking a device turns automatic switching off, as a click in the panel does, and a device that isn't connected stops the shortcut with its name ([#57](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/57)).
- Three new URLs turn automatic switching on, off or back and forth from Shortcuts, Raycast, a Stream Deck or Terminal: `audioprioritybar://enable-automatic`, `audioprioritybar://disable-automatic` and `audioprioritybar://toggle-automatic`. Settings › Shortcuts lists them with a Copy button ([#56](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/56)).

## Look

- The app has its own icon: headphones, a speaker and a microphone fanned out, with sound waves ([#58](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/58)).

## License

- Audio Priority Bar is now licensed under the GNU General Public License v3.0 ([#59](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/59)).

## Updates

- Updating from 2.9.0 or later downloads only what changed. Older versions download the full archive.

## Install

```bash
brew install --cask camguillory/tap/audio-priority-bar
```

Alternatively, download `AudioPriorityBar.zip` and `AudioPriorityBar.zip.sha256` below into the same folder, verify the archive, and move the app to `/Applications`:

```bash
shasum -a 256 -c AudioPriorityBar.zip.sha256
```

The release is universal for Apple silicon and Intel. It is signed with the project's own certificate, not an Apple Developer ID, and not notarized. If macOS blocks the first launch, open **System Settings > Privacy & Security** and click **Open Anyway**.

Connecting a Bluetooth device from the panel asks for Bluetooth permission, and Accessibility is optional, for the hover preview. Jabra Link monitoring may request Input Monitoring permission. Link 380 is hardware-verified. Link 390 is expected to work through the same capability check but remains unverified on hardware, and monitoring fails open when the link state cannot be read.
